newsitem.title: USA: DLJ cuts online stock trade commissions.
newsitem.headline: DLJ cuts online stock trade commissions.

text.p: Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc said Tuesday it has significantly expanded its on-line brokerage service and reduced commissions for on-line transactions to a flat fee of $20.
The firm also said the nine-year-old service, PC Financial Network -- http://www.pcfn.com, has been renamed DLJ Direct.
It said DLJ Direct will now offer qualified on-line investors an opportunity to invest in DLJ lead-managed initial public offerings as well as limited access to the firm's equity research.

"These changes make DLJ the first major investment bank to offer on-line investors access to a comprehensive range of its own trading services, investment research and financial products," the firm claimed in a statement.

"DLJ pioneered on-line investing with the launch of PCFN in 1988 as a no-frills, on-line discount broker," the statement continued. "We currently have more than 320,000 on-line accounts that hold more than $3.2 billion of assets."

It said "The enhancements announced today, however, represent a new level of innovation and make DLJ the only major investment bank to have chosen such a deliberate, segmented approach to serving the needs of its individual clients."

The firm said DLJ Direct is geared for the sophisticated and active, but self-directed, investor. It is available to users of the Internet, members of America Online Inc, Prodigy, CompuServe Corp, Microsoft Corp's Microsoft Investor and Reuters Holdings Plc's Reuters Money Network.

Effective June 20, DLJ Direct will charge on-line investors a flat fee of $20 for stock transactions, placing DLJ's on-line brokerage among the more competitively priced services in the marketplace, the firm said.

Also beginning this summer, investors who maintain an appropriate level of assets in their on-line accounts will be able to invest in DLJ lead-managed initial public offerings. Starting in September, qualified on-line investors will also be able to gain time-delayed access to earnings estimates, research summaries and economic analysis prepared by DLJ's equity analysts, the firm continued.

"With the introduction of research and initial public offerings, DLJ Direct becomes the first on-line brokerage service to provide customers with a comprehensive range of proprietary investment products," said K. Blake Darcy, Chief Executive Officer of DLJ Direct.
